title: ETL vs ELT: Moving Data You Can Trust
summary: What extract, transform and load each do, why modern warehouses often load first and transform later, and the properties every pipeline needs: idempotency, auditability and explicit rejects.
takeaways: ETL transforms before loading. ELT loads raw data first and transforms inside the warehouse.
Make every run idempotent: re-running the same input must produce the same result, never duplicates.
Never drop bad rows silently. Route them to a rejects table with a reason.
Dedup and upsert on a business key, keeping the latest version of each record.

steps.label: Extract
steps.detail: Read the source exactly as delivered (CSV export, API, database dump) without changing it.

steps.label: Validate
steps.detail: Check types and required fields. Send failures to rejects with a reason.

steps.label: Transform
steps.detail: Normalize formats, standardize codes and dedup to the latest version per key.

steps.label: Load (upsert)
steps.detail: Insert new keys and update changed ones, so re-runs are safe.

steps.label: Audit
steps.detail: Record counts extracted, loaded and rejected for every run.

terms.definition: Extract, Transform, Load: data is cleaned and reshaped before it lands in the target system.
Extract, Load, Transform: raw data lands first and is transformed inside the warehouse, often with SQL.
An operation that can be repeated with the same input without changing the result after the first run.
Insert a row, or update it if a row with the same key already exists.
The identifier meaningful to the business (e.g. order_id) used to recognize the same record across loads.
A warehouse table of measurable events (orders, payments) at a declared grain, linked to descriptive dimension tables.
